Central Limit Theorem:
• Sample mean L𝑋 ~𝒩𝜇, 𝜎"/𝑛
• If we know 𝜇 and 𝜎", we can compute probabilities on
sample mean L𝑋 of a given sample size 𝑛
In real life:
• Yes, the CLT still holds. It always holds!
• But we often don’t know 𝜇 or 𝜎" of our original distribution
• However, we can collect data (a sample of size 𝑛)
• How can we estimate the values 𝜇 and 𝜎" from our sample? And how 
reliable are those estimates?
